title: Learning in Structured Stackelberg Games
abstract: arXiv:2504.09006v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We initiate the study of structured Stackelberg games, a novel form of strategic interaction between a leader and a follower where contextual information can be predictive of the follower's (unknown) type. Motivated by applications such as security games and AI safety, we show how this additional structure can help the leader learn a utility-maximizing policy in both the online and distributional settings. In the online setting, we first prove that standard learning-theoretic measures of complexity do not characterize the difficulty of the leader's learning task. Notably, we find that there exists a learning-theoretic measure of complexity, analogous to the Littlestone dimension in online classification, that tightly characterizes the leader's instance-optimal regret. translated_abstract: 我们开创了对结构化Stackelberg博弈的研究，这是一种领导者与跟随者之间策略互动的新形式，其中上下文信息可以预测跟随者的（未知）类型。受安全博弈和AI安全等应用的启发，我们展示了这种额外的结构如何帮助领导者在在线和分布两种设定下学习效用最大化的策略。在在线设定中，我们首先证明了标准的学习理论复杂度度量并不能刻画领导者学习任务的难度。值得注意的是，我们发现存在一种学习理论复杂度度量，类似于在线分类中的Littlestone维度，能够紧密刻画领导者的实例最优遗憾。我们将其命名为Stackelberg-Littlestone维度，并利用它提供了一种可证明最优的在线学习算法。在分布设定中，我们……
tldr: 本文开创性地提出结构化Stackelberg博弈框架，发现了一种类似Littlestone维度的“Stackelberg-Littlestone维度”来精确刻画领导者学习任务的实例最优遗憾，并据此设计了可证明最优的在线学习算法。
en_tdlr: This paper initiates the study of structured Stackelberg games and introduces the Stackelberg-Littlestone dimension, analogous to the Littlestone dimension, which tightly characterizes the leader's instance-optimal regret and enables a provably optimal online learning algorithm.
